items.prompt: Golden tree A(B(C(E,-),-),D): D is A's right child and lands at y = 2. Swap the names A and C (tree C(B(A(E,-),-),D)). Where does D land now?
items.explain: D is the root's right child, so it starts at the same x as C and falls onto the highest thing under its 3-wide footprint. B is 3 high and sticks out under D, so the skyline there is 3, not C's 2. D lands at (0,3), the box grows to 9x4 = 36 and a hole of 2 squares is left above C.

items.prompt: In tree C(B(A(E,-),-),D), A is at (4,0) and is 3 wide. Where does its left child E start?
items.explain: A left child is next door: x = parent.x + parent.w = 4 + 3 = 7. E lands at (7,0). A right child would keep x = 4.

items.prompt: A left child always has the same y as its parent.
items.explain: Only x is copied from the parent; y comes from the skyline. In A(B(C(-,D(E,-)),-),-) with A turned, D is at (4,2) and its left child E falls to (7,0): nothing is under it.

items.prompt: Placing the right child before the left subtree gives the same packing for every tree on A to E.
items.explain: The course walks node, whole left subtree, then right child. With the other order, 1764 of the 5040 trees pack differently. In A(B(C(-,E),D),-) the box is 7x5 left first but 7x8 right first.

items.prompt: A(B(C(D(E,-),-),-),-) puts all five blocks in one row: 3+2+2+3+2 = 12 wide, but the outline is 10 wide. Which single block, turned 90 degrees, makes the row fit?
items.explain: Turning D makes it 1x3, so the row is 3+2+2+1+2 = 10 wide: the box is 10x3 = 30 and legal. Turning C or E changes nothing (they are squares), and turning A only saves 1 (11 wide).

items.prompt: Start tree A(B(C(D,-),-),E) has a 10x4 box (area 40). Which swap of two names gives the golden 9x3 box (area 27)?
items.explain: swap(D, E) gives A(B(C(E,-),-),D), the golden tree. Of the ten possible swaps it is the only one that reaches 27; the next best is swapping A and D with 30, and the rest give 40 to 50.

items.prompt: Some single swap, turn or leaf move of the golden tree gives a bounding box smaller than 27.
items.explain: All 10 swaps, all 5 turns and all 8 leaf moves give 27 or more (4 swaps, 2 turns and 1 move keep exactly 27). The golden tree is tidy, but a better tree is more than one step away (216 legal trees beat it).

items.prompt: The five blocks have a total area of 23. What is the smallest bounding-box area any of the 5040 trees can reach?
items.explain: 23 is prime, so a rectangle of area 23 would be 1x23 or 23x1, but block B is 3 high. The best is 6x4 = 24 (1 wasted square), reached by 8 trees, for example A(D,C(E(B,-),-)) where B is lifted onto D.
